Father's Day at Southfield

Father's Day often reads as the quieter half of the calendar. Southfield pushed the other way: an activation built on noise, games and shared moments that made dads the centre of the show.

participants

2,600

industry

Retail & Malls

event type

Brand Activation

location

Southfield Mall, Nairobi
The challenge
The brief was to attract families during a traditionally quiet Sunday — and to give fathers a genuine reason to bring the family out rather than stay home and watch the match.
What we did
We built a Father’s Day festival: a mini-kart circuit on the concourse, a karaoke stage with dad-friendly anthems, a tool-and-tinker workshop for hands-on kids, and a wall where dads shared their best stories. Family heats ran all day in timed slots, and the prize ladder (mall vouchers, sponsored prizes) kept repeat visits flowing. The concourse layout was planned with the mall team to keep the kart safety zone clear, and the full festival was installed overnight. The mall drew 2,600 visitors for the day — a 31% lift over a normal Sunday — with the karaoke stage packed from 2pm to close. Dwell time stretched 19% and electronics and hobby retailers reported their best Sunday of the year.
The result
The kart circuit became the day's hero, with more than 800 family heats finished, and Southfield turned Father's Day into one of its busiest Sundays of the year.
